title: HTML entity unescaping can make visible text disappear
reasoning: _html_to_text unescapes entities before stripping tags. Escaped user-visible text such as `2 < 3 and 4 > 1` becomes `2 < 3 and 4 > 1`, then _strip_html treats the `< ... >` span as an HTML tag and removes it. This corrupts generated plain-text bodies and snippets for normal HTML content containing escaped angle brackets.
recommendation: Strip actual HTML tags before entity-unescaping the remaining text, or replace the custom stripper with an HTML parser that preserves text nodes and then unescapes text content.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: tests/test_email_parser.py only covers a plain-text message body and does not exercise HTML-to-text conversion or escaped angle-bracket entities.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an HTML-only message containing `2 < 3 and 4 > 1` and assert extract_body/create_summary preserves `2 < 3 and 4 > 1` in the text/snippet.
minimumFixScope: Change _html_to_text ordering or parsing so entity decoding happens after tag removal on text content.
